title: Embedding & Reranking: Capacity Drop and Model Regression Postmortem
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~03:05 UTC the embeddings/reranking endpoint experienced a capacity drop followed by a model quality regression for a subset of customers using the high-throughput rerank path. Symptoms included elevated 5xx errors (502/503), increased tail latency for embeddings requests, and degraded NDCG scores on reranking evaluation sets. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations performed, and long-term actions to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~12 minutes of degraded availability for 18% of requests routed to high-throughput GPU pools; overall hosted API success rate dropped from 99.95% to 98.6% for embeddings/rerank during the incident window. Three paying customers reported visible reranking quality regressions on production traffic and one internal Canary flagged an automated quality alert.
timeline: 2026-03-10T03:04:30Z - Canary alert: rerank quality regression (NDCG delta > 5%) detected by eval-runner for model v2-embedded-quant8
2026-03-10T03:05:10Z - Increased 502/503 errors reported by downstream service (console/ingestion). Latency spikes observed in dashboard (p95 embeddings latency from 180ms to 610ms)
2026-03-10T03:06:00Z - Auto-scaling did not provision additional instances for dedicated high-throughput pool due to quota exhaustion on the GPU autoscaler component
2026-03-10T03:07:30Z - Traffic fallback to lower-tier model variant disabled by a recent routing config change (rollout: canary->stable) which removed a compatibility alias
2026-03-10T03:09:00Z - Mitigation 1: Rolled back routing config to re-enable fallback to model v2-embedded-fp16; errors dropped and p95 latency began to recover
2026-03-10T03:12:00Z - Mitigation 2: Manually increased autoscaler GPU quota for the pool and restarted the GPU pool controller to recover prefix KV cache pressure
2026-03-10T03:16:00Z - Incident declared resolved after stability observed for 15 continuous minutes; post-incident monitoring window opened
root_cause: Multiple contributing factors: (1) A regression in a recent kernel selection heuristic (runtime-1.22) caused a subset of model variants (quant8 pipeline) to run on a slower kernel path, increasing per-token latency and KV cache pressure. (2) The autoscaler had a bug where quota checks for dedicated GPU pools used stale quota metadata, preventing scale-up during the spike. (3) A rollout change removed an alias that allowed automatic fallback to a compatible FP16 variant, eliminating an automatic graceful degradation path.
short_term_mitigations: Rolled back routing change to re-enable fallback aliases
Manually increased autoscaler quota and restarted pool controller
Temporarily pinned affected customers to the FP16 model variant via header override
Added emergency runbook steps to the oncall playbook for embedded rerank incidents
long_term_action_items: ENG-9189: Fix autoscaler quota caching and add immediate consistency checks (owner: infra-autoscale)
ENG-9190: Revert and rework kernel selection heuristic; add offline benchmarks for quantized kernels (owner: runtime-team)
ENG-9191: Reintroduce routing compatibility aliases and add contract tests to prevent removal without test coverage (owner: routing)
ENG-9192: Add golden evals to canary pipeline that exercise embeddings/rerank critical path and fail rollout on NDCG regressions over threshold
ENG-9193: Implement per-pool emergency scale-up button in Console for SREs and oncall
ENG-9194: Capacity planning: reserve 10% burst capacity for high-throughput rerank pools during peak windows
monitoring_changes: Create dashboard panel: rerank_kv_cache_eviction_rate by pool
Add alert: embedding_p95 > 400ms for 5m with customer-impact label
Add automated rollback trigger on canary: NDCG delta > 3%
postmortem_summary: We experienced a capacity and quality incident driven by a coupling of a runtime kernel regression, an autoscaler consistency bug, and a routing change that removed graceful fallback. Short-term mitigations restored service quickly, but the event exposed gaps in testing (no golden rerank evals in canary), autoscaler observability, and routing change safeguards. Owners and timelines for remediations are listed in long_term_action_items. Expected completion for high-priority fixes is within the next two sprints.
